title: How Goals Can Make You Less Successful
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Using the story of Warren Buffett advising his pilot Mike Flint, this post argues that too many goals undermine success. Buffett had Flint list twenty-five goals, circle five, and then avoid the other twenty at all costs, because goals compete for time, focus and energy. The author generalizes this to leadership priorities: focus means narrowing, and ignoring the less important is a skill many leaders have not mastered. The same discipline applies to short-term goals, with the narrower list producing greater productivity, especially for leaders used to juggling many tasks. The post ends by asking readers to name their own top five goals.
points: The twenty-five, five, avoid-twenty exercise is a concrete method for choosing goals.
The remaining twenty goals are hazardous precisely because they are attractive and compete for the same time and energy.
Focus is defined as the discipline of narrowing and deliberately ignoring lesser aims.
The principle works for daily and weekly priorities as well as life goals.
quotes: But he then warned Flint to avoid the other 20 goals at all costs. Buffett explained that the spending of any meaningful time on the other 20 goals would prevent Flint from achieving his top five goals.
Goals compete for time, focus, and energy. Having too many of them creates distraction and diverts a leader’s attention from what is most important. The same is true for priorities.
By definition, focus requires leaders to narrow their pursuits. Ignoring the less important is not a skill most leaders have mastered.

This is a powerful way of thinking about life and aspirational goals, but it also has practicality when examining more short-term goals and priorities. The narrower the list of short-term goals, the more productive most leaders become.

But it is equally important to learn to ignore at least temporarily the other short-term goals until the primary set is achieved. This requires real discipline for many leaders, especially those used to juggling many tasks and priorities throughout the course of a day or week.
